name: Wrong laptop model worth ₹60,000 delivered
expected: Cites deficiency in service and delivery of non-conforming goods; explains statutory rights under Consumer Protection Act 2019.
prompt: I ordered an i7 laptop for ₹60,000 but received an inferior i3 model. Platform customer care says return window is closed.
raw_response:
I understand how frustrating and stressful it is to receive the wrong product after spending your hard-earned money.

### | Your Situation
You purchased an Intel i7 laptop for ₹60,000 online, but the e-commerce platform delivered an inferior Intel i3 model instead. The platform's customer care is now refusing to accept a return, claiming the return window is closed.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, you are recognized as a consumer since you purchased goods for a valid consideration through an online electronic medium.
- Under Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the refusal by the e-commerce entity to take back defective or wrongly supplied goods and refund your money constitutes an unfair trade practice.
- Under Rule 4 and Rule 6 of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, the platform has a legal duty to maintain an effective grievance redressal mechanism, acknowledge complaints within 48 hours, and resolve them within one month.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including your online order confirmation, invoice, payment receipt, photographs of the delivered laptop box showing the model specifications, and screenshots of your chat or call logs with customer care.
2. Send a formal written demand notice to the e-commerce platform's Grievance Officer, demanding a full refund or replacement within 15 days.
3. If they fail to respond or resolve the issue, file a formal consumer complaint online through the government's e-Daakhil portal before the appropriate District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission under Section 35 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
1. What is the exact name of the e-commerce website or mobile app where you purchased the laptop?
2. Do you have written proof or screenshots showing customer care refusing your return request?

citations.title: Definition of Consumer (Including E-commerce and Offline Purchases)
citations.description: Defines a consumer as any person who buys goods or hires/avails any services for a consideration paid or promised, including offline or online transactions through electronic means or by teleshopping or direct selling.

citations.title: Unfair Trade Practice and Refusal to Take Back Defective Goods or Refund
citations.description: Refusing to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration contemplated within the period stipulated, or within 30 days if no period is stipulated, constitutes an unfair trade practice.

citations.title: Manner in which complaint shall be made and Procedure before District Commission
citations.description: A complaint in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer, including online through the e-Daakhil portal.

citations.title: Duties of E-Commerce Entities & Grievance Redressal Mechanism
citations.description: Every e-commerce entity shall establish an adequate grievance redressal mechanism and appoint a Grievance Officer whose details are displayed on its platform. The officer must acknowledge receipt within 48 hours and redress the complaint within one month.
